heading: What the browser transport allows
body:
The browser transport of Dart, Rust, Go, C# and F# clients has fixed limits, so one page cannot flood the server or read too much:

- A request, with its path, query, headers and body, may hold at most 64 KiB (65,536 bytes); a larger one fails with `HTTP_REQUEST`. An answer may hold at most 1 MiB. A larger answer fails with `HTTP_LIMIT`.
- A page may have at most 64 requests waiting at the same time; one more fails with `HTTP_CAPACITY`. A request waits at most 60 seconds.
- The request must go to the origin of the page. Another origin fails with `HTTP_ORIGIN`. A redirect fails too.
- The browser sends no cookies and no other credentials. The transport refuses the headers `Cookie`, `Host`, `Origin`, `Referer`, `Connection`, `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding`, and every header that starts with `Sec-` or `Proxy-`, with `HTTP_HEADER`.
- A request is not kept in the browser cache, except a public read marked `Cached`. A request with an `Authorization` header is never kept.

An answer that does not have the shape of the model fails with `HTTP_RESPONSE`, and an answer with an error status fails with `HTTP_STATUS`. Removing the component that started a request cancels it (ADR 0090).
